title: Welcome   (title card)
text: Thank you for agreeing to be the nuclear industry’s case study for this. I want to show you two things today. First, exactly what we’ve agreed: the AI tutor running on your Export Control course, and what it gives each employee and each manager. Then, briefly, where this goes: the complete platform the same method grows into.

title: One idea   (proposal hero)
text: The whole thing rests on one idea. Every employee gets a North Star: the role they want to reach next. Every course they take builds evidence of what they’ve mastered and closes the gap to that role. And when you add those individual North Stars up across the workforce, you get the company’s North Star: who is ready, who needs support, and whether you’ll have the people each SMR needs. Personal ambition and company goals pulling in the same direction.

title: EXP-100 in eight subsections
text: We chose Export Control deliberately. Everyone at Rolls-Royce SMR takes it, because everyone handles controlled nuclear technology in some form. So from day one it gives you comparable evidence about every single employee. We’ve broken it into eight subsections. For each one we’ve listed the misconceptions people typically bring with them, and mapped the competencies it gives evidence for.

title: The tutor asks, it doesn’t tell   (demand ladder)
text: This is the heart of the AI Tutoring Tool, which we’ve co-developed with PA Consulting. When someone gets something wrong, it doesn’t give them the answer. It steps down a ladder of questions until it finds the exact point where their understanding breaks, then climbs back up so they state the right answer themselves. That’s the difference between completing a course and mastering it. And how far down the ladder they had to go, and how long it took, is itself evidence we can use.

title: The Learning Zone   (now viewing as an employee)
text: Let’s see it as an employee sees it. This is the Learning Zone, where they find all their courses. On screen is EXP-100, with the tutor built in: about 70 minutes, in short sections.

title: A tutor beside every step
text: We’re in section four, intangible transfer. An engineer is about to email pump drawings to a supplier in Czechia, and the learner has to decide what he should do before they can move on. On the right is the tutor. It opens by asking what the learner already thinks, so it knows where they’re starting from. Along the top you can see its four stages: diagnose, confront and correct, prove, retain. And the counters: confident answers, unsure answers, and misconceptions still open.

title: Wrong, and sure   (the demo answers the question)
text: Watch our learner. ‘No, they’re our own drawings.’ And they’re sure. This is exactly the belief that causes real breaches. A confident wrong answer is the most valuable thing the tutor can find.

title: A diagnosis
text: The tutor has tagged it: misconception S4a, ‘emailing a colleague in our own company is never an export’. That stays private to the learner. It has to be safe to be wrong here, or people stop saying when they’re unsure. Now look at what it says back. No answer. A question that makes them look at their own thinking again. Here it asks: the email starts in our system. Where are the drawings once the supplier opens them?

title: Points to the course
text: The learner asks for help. The tutor quotes the exact line of your approved course and asks which answer it points to. It only ever uses your content, and the learner still does the work.

title: Proved, and resolved
text: Second attempt: right, and confident. S4a is marked resolved. If they’d been right but unsure, the tutor would count that as fragile and bring it back in spaced reviews at one, three and six weeks. So when someone finishes this course, they haven’t just clicked through. They’ve mastered it, and they can prove it.

title: Every employee sets their own learning needs   (the settings panel opens)
text: Now something that matters for a workforce as varied as yours. Every employee can set how the platform works for them, once, in My learning needs. There are quick-start options for dyslexia, low vision, colour blindness, deafness, focus, a calm display, another language and motor needs, and each one can be fine-tuned. With the person’s consent, HR can record adjustments when they join, so everything is ready on their first day.

title: Reading and seeing, adapted   (Aisha’s settings applied)
text: Here Aisha has chosen dyslexia-friendly reading and colour-blind safe colours. The font, spacing and background change, a reading ruler follows the pointer, and the key points come first. Every colour-coded result now carries a tick, a cross or a pattern, so nothing depends on colour alone.

title: Deaf and hard of hearing   (sign-language pop-up)
text: For deaf and hard-of-hearing colleagues, every video has captions and a transcript, and a qualified interpreter signs each step in their own sign language: British Sign Language here, Czech Sign Language at Temelín, Swedish Sign Language in Sweden. The tutor panel flashes for new messages instead of relying on sound.

title: Learning in their own language   (Czech translation)
text: And a colleague at Temelín can learn in Czech. The step, the quizzes and the tutor all switch language, with the English one tap away, because the English wording stays the authoritative version for export-controlled content. That’s what makes this fair: everyone is measured on what they understand, not on how well the page suits them.

title: Aisha’s North Star   (learner dashboard)
text: This is what an employee sees when they sign in. Aisha is a Buyer. Her North Star is Head of Procurement. She can see the whole route, the next rung, and two scores: how her knowledge measures up for her next step, and for her North Star. They move every time she completes a section. They measure knowledge only; experience and SQEP sign-off are judged separately. For most people, this is the first time anyone has shown them a clear path, with evidence.

title: She knows exactly how she performed
text: This is the promise we made about the tutor. After every section, Aisha gets plain feedback: what she did well, the misconceptions she’s cleared, and the three things to work on next. Each one says why it matters for the role she wants, and links straight back to practise it with the tutor. No guessing about where she stands.

title: Strengths and aptitude
text: Here’s her competency profile against what her next step and her North Star need. And underneath, something no completion report shows: how she learns. How often her answers are secure, how many misconceptions she’s cleared, how many without hints. That’s aptitude, measured rather than assumed.

title: A route, and the courses that close the gap
text: Every rung has a readiness score. The courses recommended are the ones that close her specific gaps. And ‘where your strengths point’ shows other job families her evidence fits. It suggests; it never decides. Everything here informs a development conversation. Nothing makes a selection decision.

title: Mastery, not completion   (now viewing as a manager)
text: Now the manager. Every person, every subsection. Green is mastered, amber developing, red not yet. What each person gets wrong while they’re learning stays private to them. The manager sees results. And the flags on the right show where someone’s evidence sits below what their current role needs. Today most managers get a tick box that says ‘completed’. This tells them what their people actually understand.

title: Where to act, and who is ready
text: On the left, hotspots: the misconceptions the team shares, shown only when three or more people share one, and never by name. If three people think a video call isn’t a transfer, one ten-minute briefing fixes it for all of them. On the right, how close each person’s knowledge is to the next rung on their own North Star.

title: Ten staff, live   (simulation starts)
text: Let’s watch it happen. Ten staff working through EXP-100. On the left, each event from the tutor. In the middle, North Star turning that event into evidence, a level, readiness and a recommendation, in seven steps.

title: Insights
text: As patterns emerge, insights go to the right person. Someone reaching mastery. A team hotspot. Someone whose knowledge is now ready for a next step.

title: The live dashboard
text: And the manager’s view fills in as it happens. No waiting for an end-of-quarter report.

title: Is everyone on course?   (tracker)
text: This is where it becomes about potential. Across: how fast someone is progressing compared with the pace their North Star needs. Up: how ready they are. On the right, people pulling ahead. On the left, people falling behind. You see both after one course, not after an annual review.

title: Early intervention
text: Tom is flagged for a North Star review. The manager sees his planned route, where he’ll land at his current pace, and a specific suggestion. They agree a change together, and it’s recorded. That’s early intervention with the fix attached.

title: Spot potential early
text: And Hannah is accelerating. Her evidence says she’s ahead of her plan, so the suggestion is to stretch her North Star, before she starts looking elsewhere. That’s the clarity we promised: each person knows their potential, and so does their manager.

title: Now the platform   (title card)
text: Everything you’ve seen so far runs on one course. North Star is Developing Experts’ platform, and it is built to do much more. Now imagine the same method across every course, every person and every SMR. I know you’re planning your own learning platform next year, so let me show you what that could look like.

title: Pathways
text: Eleven job families built from the roles you’re advertising, five levels each, with the courses at every level. They all start from a shared core that begins with EXP-100.

title: The tutor on every course
text: Classroom, blended or e-learning, every course can have the tutor alongside it. Each one feeds the same North Star.

title: Your own courses   (Course studio)
text: Your learning team builds and publishes its own courses here, with a proper review and approval flow. Or imports finished courses from us. Nothing reaches staff until it’s approved.

title: Every new course feeds North Star
text: And this is what keeps it rigorous. Before a course can be published, the checks make sure it has tutor questions, wrong answers tagged with misconceptions, and competencies mapped. So every course you add makes everyone’s profile richer, automatically.

title: Staffing every SMR   (now viewing as workforce and finance)
text: Now the company’s North Star. For each SMR in the programme, the planner shows how many of your people it needs, and how many North Star already rates as ready. Commission a new SMR here and the plan appears in seconds.

title: An SMR is ordered: add it in a minute   (commission form opens)
text: And when you sign a new order, your admin team adds the SMR here: its name, site, customer and dates. The moment they do, North Star shows how many people it will need and how many to recruit, sets its staffing quota from your standard template, and raises the draft course orders. From contract to a people plan in about a minute.

title: Ready, upskill, promote or recruit
text: For every job family: who’s ready now, who can be upskilled, who can be promoted, and who you’ll have to recruit. This is exactly where each employee’s North Star meets the company’s. Aisha’s progress shows up here as a promotion you don’t have to hire for.

title: Which courses, and when
text: For each gap, it shows which course people need, groups them into cohorts, and gives a date to book it by. That date is counted back from when each person starts in post, so they’re trained before they start, not after.

title: Quota for each SMR
text: Each SMR has a set number of posts by domain and level. North Star fills them from your existing people first, and shows what must be recruited. The numbers are marked as estimates until you confirm them.

title: One timeline
text: Recruitment, notice periods, security clearance and training, worked back from each in-post date.

title: Risks
text: And the risks generated straight from the plan: late hires, clearance delays, scarce skills.

title: One place for what needs attention
text: All of it comes together on one page for your admin team, most urgent first.

title: From one course to every course   (back to the proposal)
text: So the path is simple. The case study proves the method on EXP-100. Then we add the mandatory core, then specialist pathways, then leadership. The platform stays the same; only the content grows. And the level of evidence rises from practitioner up to expert and leader.

title: Delivery plan
text: We’ve timed it to your move to your own platform: discovery, build, a pilot with one cohort, then roll-out, so by next year North Star can simply become your platform.

title: The close   (title card)
text: So, what this pilot gives you. Every employee knows exactly how they performed and what to do next. Every manager sees mastery, potential and aptitude, not just completion. And the organisation can see who is ready for each new SMR, and what it will take to close the gap. Each person’s North Star, aligned to Rolls-Royce SMR’s. What I’d like to agree today is the pilot cohort and how we’ll measure success.
